$comment: Single source for the participant card (CARD.md) and the hub (hub/index.html). Edit this file, then run npm run card. npm run card:check fails when the generated files are out of date. Plain English, one idea per sentence.
title: Workshop 5 · AI-native SDLC with Claude Code

start.say: Install Claude Code with the official instructions at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup, then create this isolated starter. Terminal 1 starts Claude Code after the lifecycle introduction and before code edits; terminal 2 configures the SDK and runs the lab.

assistant.title: Claude Code first minutes
assistant.prompt: Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and CARD.md. Explain the AI SDLC we will practise, its required artifacts and human decisions. Distinguish your development role from the runtime SRE agent. Name the two starter exercises. Do not edit files or run approval, execution, mitigation, resolution, commit or push commands. Wait for my review.

start.see: ✓ SDK preflight passes before fault injection, then the lab runs. Hub: http://127.0.0.1:4320/hub · Console: http://127.0.0.1:4320 · Shop: http://127.0.0.1:4310.
start.check: `curl 127.0.0.1:4320/api/health` shows `"mode":"healthy"` and the selected model. `npm run model:check` must return READY before a real-model fault injection.
stuck: Port 4310 or 4320 is already in use
Another copy runs. Stop only your own workshop launcher with Ctrl+C in its terminal. Never kill an unknown process.
Install Node 22 or newer. Check with `node --version`.
The console header says no telemetry
Wait 20 seconds. The shop writes telemetry every few seconds while traffic runs.
Report the missing API/provider configuration. Use `npm start -- --fast --offline` only as an explicit fallback; it is not model evidence. See `docs/claude-code.md`.
start.why: Practise a software delivery cycle on a local SRE agent. Claude Code helps develop the software; the separate runtime agent reads the shop telemetry. Humans accept plans, review evidence and authorize release.

cores.name: Specify a change from evidence
cores.goal: Observe the failing checkout and verify the diagnosis. Turn the missing deployment evidence into an accepted software requirement.
cores.slides: Specify: start with an observed problem · Create one fault and observe detection · Check the diagnosis against the evidence · Turn the finding into an intent · Accept the assignment before building

steps.do: Break the shop once: click `Bad deploy v2.15.0` in the shop. The CLI alternative is `npm run chaos -- deploy v2.15.0 --mode bad-deploy` in a separate shell, never the occupied launcher terminal. Do not use both.
steps.see: After about one minute a new incident appears in the console sidebar. You did not open it; the deterministic listener did.
steps.stuck: No incident after three minutes: look at the lab terminal. Traffic must print requests. Started without `--fast`? Then detection takes five minutes.
steps.before: Telemetry is recorded service data. The listener opens an incident when server metrics cross a fixed limit; no model makes that decision.

steps.do: Open the incident. Read the banner at the top, then the diagnosis.
steps.see: The model output may vary. Expect missing deploy evidence, a verified tool trace and explicit data gaps; the starter cannot see the deploy.
steps.check: Preserve the diagnosis and trace. Verify every cited reference in `demo/data/telemetry.json`, then search that file for `v2.15.0`: there WAS a deploy outside the starter's visible tool result.
steps.stuck: References are text, not links. Search the file for the timestamp.
steps.before: An evidence reference points to an observation. A data gap means unknown, not proof that nothing happened.

steps.do: Challenge the agent in chat: Could this be something other than the deployment?
steps.see: Real output may vary. With the explicit offline fallback, the agent returns a scripted summary; that is not a new model investigation.
steps.check: Compare the answer with `ruled_out`, the trace and the data gap.
steps.stuck: If it fabricates a deploy citation or fails the contract, preserve the output and stop; do not call it success or weaken the contract.
steps.before: Free-text chat is not checked by the structured verdict contract. Verify its claims manually against telemetry and trace; use Investigate for a contract-validated diagnosis.

steps.do: Save the diagnosis in `docs/diagnosis-live.md`. Then record what you checked: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 1: <what you verified>"`
steps.see: One new line at the bottom of `PROGRESS.md`.
steps.check: Your note names the references you checked, not only that you did it.
steps.stuck: Do not approve. There is nothing safe to execute yet. Core 2 gives the agent its eyes back.
steps.before: A progress note records a check you performed. It is history, not a test result by itself.

steps.do: Ask Claude Code: "Read docs/diagnosis-live.md and intent.md. Draft a scoped intent for the missing deployment evidence and human gate. Name observable acceptance checks and an open question. Do not edit code or approve anything. Wait for my review."
steps.before: An intent defines the outcome before the implementation. An acceptance check states what another person can observe, not that the agent feels confident.
steps.see: A draft `intent.md` with a user, problem, outcome, constraints and an open question. Checks cover returned deploys, empty data and the named-human gate.
steps.check: Review every check yourself. Link each to a test or recorded observation. Reject fabricated evidence or a plan to weaken the contract. Record your name and acceptance decision in `intent.md`.
steps.stuck: Use the existing intent template. Ask Claude to clarify one vague check. Do not proceed to code until you accept the scope.

cores.why: The agent needs an observable goal and a boundary before it writes code. An incident diagnosis is input to that decision, not the requirement itself.
cores.proof: docs/diagnosis-live.md contains checked observations. intent.md states the user, outcome, acceptance checks, boundary, open question and your acceptance decision.

cores.name: Design, build and verify the change
cores.goal: Review a human plan before each repair. Restore the read-only tool and the approval gate, then verify the complete change.
cores.slides: Establish a reviewable starting point · Ask for a small plan, then review it · Understand the tool before repair · Repair the tool: red → green · Check the change on the same incident · Understand the human approval gate · Repair the gate: refuse unsafe actions · Verify the complete change

steps.do: Before code edits, follow the human-only baseline commands in `docs/sdlc-git.md`. In the isolated starter, create `workshop-base`, commit only the two exercise cuts, then create `fix/w5-core`.
steps.before: The checkpoint has a solved HEAD plus unfinished exercise cuts. Without a baseline commit, restoring the solution could leave an empty code diff.
steps.see: `git branch --show-current` prints `fix/w5-core`. The `workshop-base` commit contains only the A5 and A8 starter cuts.
steps.check: Inspect `git show --stat workshop-base`. It lists only `src/tools.ts` and `src/executor.ts`. Keep intent and evidence edits outside this baseline commit.
steps.stuck: Do not overwrite an existing branch or commit someone else's work. Ask the facilitator if either branch name already exists. Claude must not run the baseline commands.

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`. Ask Claude Code: "Read intent.md, docs/spec.md and the failing test. Propose the smallest change in docs/plan.md. Name files, checks, risks, a rejected alternative and your stop point. Do not edit code. Wait for my review."
steps.see: The test fails: `list_deploys` returns nothing. `npm run bench` fails too: without deploys the agent misses the bad deploy.
steps.check: Explain the failing assertion. Review the plan against your intent and the existing contract. Record your accepted scope in `docs/plan.md` before implementation.
steps.stuck: Find the single `TODO(A5)` handler stub in `src/tools.ts`. Restore the read-only handler binding; inspect and preserve the existing MCP registration.
steps.before: A red test exposes the missing behaviour. The bench checks scripted outcomes across fixed scenarios, not model quality.

steps.do: Build the `list_deploys` handler in `src/tools.ts` with Claude Code or by hand. Keep the existing MCP registration intact.
steps.see: `test/workshop/tools.test.ts` is green. The A8 valid-approval executor assertion remains red until the gate repair later in Core 2.
steps.check: After plan review, implement and run `npx tsx --test test/workshop/tools.test.ts`, then `npm run typecheck` and `npm run bench`. The bench prints `PASS bench`; executor tests remain intentionally red until the gate repair later in Core 2. Save the actual commands, results and any untested paths in `docs/verify/sdlc.md`. A8 remains expected red here, so this intermediate state is not yet release-ready.
steps.stuck: The tool still returns `[]`: inspect the handler binding and the preserved registration; do not add a second registration.
steps.before: MCP exposes named tools. The existing registration points to a handler that reads data; restore that binding only after the human reviews the small plan.

steps.do: Save. In the same incident, ask in chat: `Investigate: customers report checkout errors`
steps.see: The lab terminal prints a console reload line. Inspect the new diagnosis, its observed trace, deploy references, data gaps and proposal; real model wording and actions can vary.
steps.check: Verify the actual trace and references against `demo/data/telemetry.json`. If the citation is fabricated or the contract fails, preserve the output and stop. Record what you verified: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 2: ..."`
steps.stuck: Incident gone? Incident history persists in SQLite, while the shop resets on restart. Do not restart the launcher to reload code; saving auto-reloads the console. For a fresh repeat, use a new disposable checkpoint copy; do not rebreak a stale incident.
steps.before: A trace records the tools used for a diagnosis. Re-investigation lets you compare the same incident before and after the repair.

steps.do: Run the red test: `npx tsx --test test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. Ask Claude for a fail-closed plan for `checkApproval` in `src/executor.ts`. Review that plan before allowing the `TODO(A8)` repair.
steps.see: The test is green. The executor now refuses to act without a named approval for this incident and this proposal.
steps.stuck: Read `test/workshop/executor.test.ts`. It names every case the gate must refuse. Chat refuses your sentence: that is correct for anything that changes the system. Approve, execute and resolve are buttons.
steps.before: The approval gate validates a named human decision for this incident and proposal. The starter fails closed until you rebuild it.

steps.do: Run `npx tsx --test test/workshop/executor.test.ts`, `npm run verify`, `npm run test:workshop` and `npm run test:hooks`.
steps.see: All must pass before the code release decision.
steps.stuck: If a check fails, preserve its output and do not mark the change ready for release.
steps.before: Run the complete checks after both repairs so the results cover the full change.

cores.why: A bounded plan limits accidental changes. A failing test, a passing test and a real diff show what the repair changed.
cores.proof: docs/plan.md records the reviewed plans. Both repairs have a visible diff, the same-incident trace is checked, and the complete checks pass before release review.

cores.name: Review, release and learn from the result
cores.goal: Review the complete code change, prepare its PR and record a human release decision. Observe the local runtime and propose the next improvement.
cores.slides: Review the actual diff · Prepare the PR and make a release decision · Observe runtime with separate permission · Recovery: confirmed or not confirmed? · Turn the observation into the next task

steps.do: Ask Claude Code: "Review git diff workshop-base against intent.md, docs/plan.md and REVIEW.md. Identify functional defects, missing checks and unsupported claims. Cite files and lines. Do not edit, approve, commit, push or merge. Wait for my decision."
steps.before: First run git status --short. Untracked files are absent from the diff: inspect them and stage only intended files by exact path yourself before requesting review. Never stage secrets. Review checks whether the change meets the intent, not whether its explanation sounds convincing. Passing tests do not approve a change.
steps.see: A list of findings, or an explicit no-findings result. The human has inspected the diff and evidence rather than accepting the model's conclusion.
steps.check: Verify every finding yourself. Request fixes and rerun affected checks when needed. Record your name, decision, residual risks and untested paths in `docs/verify/sdlc.md`.
steps.stuck: When working solo, review your own diff in a separate pass and record that limitation. If repository policy requires another reviewer, wait for one.

steps.do: Prepare the PR text with Claude Code, then follow `docs/sdlc-git.md` in your own terminal. A human commits, signs the Git gate, pushes to the learner repo and opens a PR from `fix/w5-core` into `workshop-base`.
steps.before: A Git approval authorizes publication of a code change. It does not approve a shop rollback. Never push the training baseline to the upstream project.
steps.see: A PR with a meaningful repair diff, accepted intent, actual checks and known limitations. If remote access or a required reviewer is missing, the record says `RELEASE BLOCKED`.
steps.check: A human checks the current head, CI and required review before merging. Record the PR and merge commit, or the exact blocker. A local reload is a development check, not a production deployment.
steps.stuck: No publication access: prepare the PR text and document the blocker. You may continue local runtime observation as a test, but must not claim a release or bypass branch protection.

steps.do: After code review, inspect the current incident and its actual proposal. Only if the evidence supports an allowed action, a named human clicks Approve and then the separate Execute control. Otherwise record the safe stop.
steps.see: For an executed rollback, the banner asks you to wait for all recovery checks. About two minutes later, inspect LANDED or NOT LANDED. A model response is not guaranteed to propose rollback.
steps.check: The half check may fail. The full and double checks must both pass. On NOT LANDED the banner names the failed check, its value and the limit.
steps.stuck: A button is grey: the banner says which step is allowed now. The server refuses every other button.
steps.before: Rollback restores the prior deployment. Recovery checks capture measured values against a frozen limit; execution success alone is insufficient.

steps.do: LANDED: click Mark mitigated, then Resolve with notes. NOT LANDED: do not close. Read the failed check, then investigate in chat or escalate.
steps.see: After you resolve, the next-step detail says Resolved and directs you to the notes and lesson. Execute stays disabled.
steps.check: If resolved, `lessons/lessons.md` has your name and the incident id. If NOT LANDED, confirm the incident remains open and retain the failed check. Record your actual outcome: `npm run progress:note -- "Core 3: …"`
steps.stuck: Never execute again to get a green result. NOT LANDED is a correct, safe stop.
steps.before: LANDED means the full and double checks passed. Mitigated and resolved are separate human decisions. NOT LANDED or unknown means stop.

steps.do: Ask Claude Code: "Read the actual observations in docs/verify/sdlc.md. Propose one next change and the acceptance check or regression test that would prove it. Distinguish observed facts from hypotheses. Do not edit code or close the incident. Wait for my review."
steps.before: Maintenance feeds the next planning cycle. A closed incident or a model-generated lesson is not automatically a reviewed software improvement.
steps.see: One proposed next task grounded in a trace, failed check, review finding or missing observation. It includes an acceptance check.
steps.check: Review the proposal yourself. Record the task, evidence and your decision in `docs/verify/sdlc.md`. Keep an unresolved incident open. Record progress with `npm run progress:note -- "SDLC: recorded actual evidence, release decision and next task"`.
steps.stuck: If the model or recovery was blocked, use that observed limitation. Do not invent a successful run. Implementing this next task is optional; proposing and reviewing it is required.

cores.why: The authoring agent cannot accept its own work. Code release and runtime recovery are different decisions, with different evidence.
cores.proof: docs/verify/sdlc.md records actual diff review, a human PR and release decision or RELEASE BLOCKED, the runtime result and one reviewed next task.

deeper.name: Read the contract
deeper.do: Write `docs/spec.md` for the evidence rules in `src/contract.ts`. Run `npx tsx --test test/contract.test.ts` and break one rule on purpose.

deeper.name: Add your own guard rule
deeper.do: Add one deny rule of your own to `.claude/hooks/guard.mjs` BY HAND (the agent may not edit hooks). Prove it with a deny line in `approvals/audit.jsonl`. Write `docs/decisions/D01-*.md`.

deeper.name: Add a bench case
deeper.do: Add one case to `bench/cases.json`, run `npm run bench`. Ask the agent to lower `bench/ratchet.json` and watch the guard deny it.

deeper.name: Your hackathon intent.md
deeper.do: Write `docs/hackathon-intent.md` for the agent you build next. Hand off with the `/handoff` skill.

checkpoints.say: The committed-HEAD starter has the A5 tool exercise and a fail-closed A8 approval gate.
Core 2 is an intermediate catch-up point: the read-only tool is solved, but the A8 approval gate remains cut. This checkpoint does not prove participant-authored work.
Core 3 is the solved reference with no exercise cuts. This checkpoint does not prove participant-authored work.

catchUp: Run `npm run checkpoint -- core-2` or `npm run checkpoint -- core-3` from the ORIGINAL, unchanged clone root, not from a modified starter. Each creates a separate current-HEAD worktree and refuses overwrite. Core 2 is an intermediate tool-solved, gate-unfinished catch-up point; Core 3 is the solved reference. Neither proves you authored, tested or reviewed a change. Compare files yourself. Never copy runtime data, approvals, progress or lesson history.

opening.title: Start with the AI SDLC
opening.why: Faster code is not enough. A useful change needs a clear outcome, checked evidence and a human release decision.
opening.loop: Plan → Design → Build → Test → Release → Observe → Plan again.
opening.proof: Produce an accepted intent, a reviewed plan, a tested diff, a human release decision and one reviewed next task.
opening.practice: We change the SRE agent and observe a local shop. These are practice systems, not the learning goal.
